Subject: Post-demo: TensorBay performance targets, test scripts & IP allowlist

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — good conversation. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get your customer-led load run scheduled: 

High-level SLO targets you confirmed on the call:
- P95 end-to-end generation latency (short prompts, <= 128 tokens): <= 250 ms
- Sustained throughput target: 500 reqs/sec across 3 regions (primary focus: us-west)
- Concurrent open streaming sessions: 120 concurrent streams (avg tokens/sec ~40)
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx across the window

What Redwood will provide before the run:
- A dedicated test account and API key scoped to TensorBay test project (expires after the run). See attached readme.
- A k6-compatible profile (attached) that models a mixed workload: 70% short-chat generation, 20% embedding/rerank, 10% long streaming sessions.
- IP egress ranges to add to your allowlist and an Ops contact reachable during the window.

What we need from you:
- Confirmation of the test window (we suggested 2026-10-07 09:00-11:00 PT, but you requested alternatives below).
- Names / emails to provision as test users (we create API keys per user for traceability).
- Any network/NAT IPs or proxy egress addresses (if you run the k6 load from managed runners) so we can coordinate allowlist and firewall rules.
- Any tokenized prompt sets you want included in the run (or we will use the safe sample set in the k6 profile).

Attachments in this message: tensorbay_k6_profile_v1.js (k6 script stub), redwood_test_account_readme.txt (credentials + instructions)

Next steps: if we agree to 10/07, Ben will provision the keys and Soojin will validate capacity and pre-warm the fleet. Can you confirm the window and provide the IPs/test user list by EOD Monday (10/04)?

Thanks,
Ethan

- Capacity reservation: request placed for 2026-10-07 00:00 UTC -> 2026-10-08 04:00 UTC to cover both proposed windows. Ops will create an extra transient pool sized for an extra 30% headroom above 500 req/s. Note that actual autoscale still applies but this gives predictable latency.
- Allowlist: confirmed — we'll accept the three egress IPs that Priya provided. Ops needs a confirmation email with exact IPs and whether you are running through NAT/proxy.
- Monitoring: I'll provision a read-only dashboard link and a trace-collection hook. Ops-on-call during the run: marissa@redwood.com (CS/ops liaison) and infra-on-call: infra-oncall@redwood.com.
